::: {#sol-euler-polynomial}

1. The values are $41$, $43$, $47$ and $53$, which are all prime.
2. Take $n = 41$:
   $41^2 + 41 + 41 = 41 \cdot (41 + 1 + 1) = 41 \cdot 43$,
   which is not prime.
   The smallest $n$ that works is $n = 40$:
   $40^2 + 40 + 41 = 1681 = 41^2$.
   For every $n$ from $0$ to $39$, $n^2 + n + 41$ is prime,
   so checking many cases did not prove the claim.

:::
